title: Four-step dimensional design process
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The four design decisions in order: select the business process, declare the grain, identify the dimensions, identify the facts.

title: Additive, semi-additive, and non-additive facts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Additive facts sum across all dimensions; balances are semi-additive (not across time); ratios are non-additive, so store the components, sum them and compute the ratio from the totals.

title: Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page updated 1 Apr 2026). Fact and dimension tables, consistent grain, explicit measures (unit price should not be summed), surrogate keys, snowflake vs single table, type 2 slowly changing dimensions need a warehouse, role-playing dimensions with cloned tables or USERELATIONSHIP; points to Kimball's Data Warehouse Toolkit.

title: Model relationships in Power BI Desktop
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 5 Sep 2025, updated 7 Oct 2026). Relationships do not enforce integrity; duplicates on the one side fail refresh; blank virtual rows (unknown members); use bi-directional filtering only as needed; many-to-many relationships are limited, use inner-join semantics and cannot use RELATED; date/time columns keep the time part.

title: Design guidance for date tables in Power BI Desktop
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 2 Jan 2026). Date table requirements: unique dates, no blanks, no missing dates, full years; mark as date table for classic time intelligence; Auto date/time only for simple calendar models.

title: Data refresh in Power BI
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 18 Sep 2026). Eight scheduled refreshes a day on shared capacity (API refreshes count, manual ones do not), 48 on Premium, PPU or Fabric; two-hour limit on shared capacity, five hours on Premium; schedule paused after two months with no visits.

title: Power BI service features by license type
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 24 Aug 2026). Free licence for own content; Pro shares with Pro; PPU shares with PPU; free users can consume content in Premium or Fabric F64 and larger capacities.

title: Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 13 May 2026). RLS applies only to the Viewer role; dynamic RLS with USERPRINCIPALNAME; roles are additive; Test as role uses your own identity for dynamic rules; RLS does not restrict columns.

title: Copilot for Power BI overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 24 Aug 2026). Requires paid Fabric F2+ or Premium P1+; Pro or PPU alone is not enough; 10,000-character prompts; answers from general knowledge when a question is not about the model; prepare data for AI first.

title: Overview of the MCP Servers (Power BI)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 24 Sep 2026). Power BI Authoring MCP server (hosted preview, local generally available) creates and changes models; Fabric IQ answers questions and respects RLS and OLS; clients act with the signed-in user's permissions; data moves to the client and its model provider.

title: Data Studio returns as new home for Data Cloud assets (11 April 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Looker Studio renamed Data Studio on 11 April 2026; existing reports moved with no action; free for individuals; Data Studio Pro is the paid team edition.

title: How blends work in Data Studio
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Up to five tables per blend; inner, left, right, full outer, cross joins and union; equality conditions only; tables grouped and aggregated before joining; identical rows collapse without an ID; blends live in one report.

title: Data credentials (Data Studio)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Owner's credentials let viewers see data without their own access; viewer's credentials require each viewer's access; service account credentials only for BigQuery in Workspace or Cloud Identity organisations.

title: Manage data freshness (Data Studio)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Default freshness: Google Analytics 12 hours (1, 4 or 12), Google Sheets 15 minutes, BigQuery and SQL sources 1 minute to 12 hours (default 12), Google marketing products fixed at 12 hours; blends use the shortest; BigQuery costs apply to each query.

title: About calculated fields (Data Studio)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Data source vs chart-specific calculated fields; chart-specific fields support blends; explicit aggregation such as SUM(Profit) / SUM(Revenue).

title: About Data Studio Pro
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Organisation-owned content linked to a Google Cloud project, team workspaces, up to 200 delivery schedules per report, alerts, Gemini features including calculated fields from plain-language prompts; 30-day trial.

title: [GA4] Data thresholds
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Thresholds are system-defined and cannot be adjusted; applied with demographics, search queries and small user counts; widening the date range may reveal data.

title: Metrics (Metabase documentation, v0.65)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A metric is a data source, an aggregation formula and dimensions; use conditional aggregations instead of filters; avoid joins in metric definitions; metrics are managed in Metabase's own Data Studio and Library.

title: Metabase pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Open Source plan is free and self-hosted; Starter, Pro and Enterprise are paid.

title: Common Pitfalls in Dashboard Design (white paper, February 2006)
supports: Opened with WebFetch and read with a text extractor. Few's working definition of a dashboard (single screen, monitored at a glance) and his list of 13 common pitfalls; based on his book Information Dashboard Design.

title: IBCS Standards
supports: Opened with WebFetch. IBCS Standards 2.0 released 11 June 2026, aligned with ISO 24896 Notation for business reporting; published free under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
supports: Opened with WebFetch. W3C Recommendation of 12 December 2024; 1.4.1 Use of Color; 1.4.3 contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 large text); 1.4.11 non-text contrast 3:1.

title: The Balanced Scorecard: Measures That Drive Performance (January–February 1992)
publisher: Harvard Business Review (Robert S. Kaplan and David P. Norton)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Authors, issue date and the article's point that what you measure is what you get.

title: OKR meaning, definition and example
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Objectives vs key results; Andy Grove at Intel, John Doerr, Google 1999; three to five key results per objective; committed vs aspirational OKRs.

title: CFPB fines Wells Fargo $100 million for widespread illegal practice of secretly opening unauthorized accounts (8 September 2016)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. $100 million fine; more than two million possibly unauthorised accounts in the bank's own analysis; employees spurred by sales targets and compensation incentives.

title: PHE statement on delayed reporting of COVID-19 cases (4 October 2020)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 15,841 cases from 25 September to 2 October 2020 left out of reported daily figures because files exceeded the maximum file size of a data load process; large files now split; dashboard corrected.

title: How Airbnb Achieved Metric Consistency at Scale
supports: Search-confirmed (fetch blocked with HTTP 403): a search result showed this exact page. Airbnb's Minerva platform manages the life cycle of metric definitions so metrics are computed consistently. Only this headline-level claim is used.

title: Tableau MCP (tableau/tableau-mcp)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Tableau's official MCP server; hosted version uses OAuth so each user signs in with their own identity; self-hosted version uses a personal access token; no read-only guarantee stated.
